title: S0 dialect 0.3: empty qreg-table image is not a positive-size ISA data symbol
description: Draft spec/Bennett-Dialect-Spec-0.3-draft.md §19.5 (line 11229) requires the positive-size __bennett_rt_qtab global to have an empty data image, citing ISA E4. §6.5 line 1773 and §24 D29 line 11742 require real records/counter storage (default up to 2^40 bytes). ISA 0.9 §9.2 lines 1991-1994 requires a same-size data symbol for every global; §9.1 encodes data as NAME SP HEX. E4/§16.1 lines 4073-4075 only permits the trailing space spelling of zero-byte data; it adds no zero-fill/BSS or sparse-image encoding for a nonempty symbol. Concrete isolated witness: a disjoint qtab global [12288,16384), declared data size 4096, and line 'qtab ' with empty HEX is rejected by the cached ISA-0.9 reference CLI as '§7.2: data size differs from signature'. title: V10 residual whitelist conflicts with retained extended-format fneg contract
description: Literal normative row in section12.4: "| V10 | an operand or result of type `half`, `bfloat`, `x86_fp80`, `fp128` or `ppc_fp128` other than in `bitcast`, `load`, `store`, `select` and `phi` (after N33) |". But section13.1 says "`fneg`, `llvm.fabs`, `llvm.copysign`, `bitcast`, `load`, `store`, `select`, `phi` | unchanged: bit-exact operations (LangRef)" for all seven formats, and section16.4 maps fneg in all carriers. New validator-v10-residue follows literal V10 and expects rejection for half fneg, while the checker accepts and the retained-operation contract supports acceptance. This is a normative conflict, not grounds to narrow extended-format support or weaken the example. Full intended V10 exception boundary (including retained intrinsics and carrier interfaces) needs reconciliation; no semantic edit made in the example-only 0.2.1 coverage job. Fix requires README semantic-version policy and council review.
notes:
Pre-edit hand derivation (2026-10-29): Reading A applies V10 literally. load half and bitcast half are exceptions, but fneg half is not, so validator-v10-residue rejects. It also rejects retained llvm.fabs/llvm.copysign and extended-format call/ret/aggregate transport; rewriting those away would contradict the unchanged row of section 13.1 and the carrier map of section 16.4. This narrows NS section 3.2's explicit promise that fneg/fabs/copysign and transport remain bit-exact. Reading B applies sections 13.1 and 13.3 uniformly to all seven formats and section 16 to their interfaces: N32/N33 remove arithmetic/comparison/conversion, not retained bit operations or transport. Thus for half bits b, fneg is b xor 0x8000, including NaN payload and quiet/signaling bits, and is accepted; residual fadd half still rejects and must become the carrier call __bennett_sf_add_f16(i16,i16). Deciding sentence: V10 must permit every bit-exact operation retained by section 13.1 and every carrier transport admitted by section 16, for all seven floating-point formats. Rule 10 selects Reading B; there are not two non-narrowing alternatives. Plan: amend V10, put fneg in the accept witness and fadd in the reject witness, add an intrinsic/interface witness, and correct the stale Appendix B conflict status. README and section 23 require the full version 0.2.2 and norm 0.2.2; unchanged map/other ABIs remain at their versions. SPEC_VERSIONS.toml and checker version synchronization are outside the owned paths and must be handled by their owner before a green full gate. No map, layout, reference object or hash changes.
Resolved in owned documents: V10 now exempts the complete section 13.1 retained bit-exact row plus section 16 parameter/call/return/aggregate transport; call exclusions V4/V9/V12 are preserved. The former fneg negative is now the positive witness; the negative retains fadd half; validator-v10-carriers exercises fabs/copysign and defined-call/return/aggregate transport. Full dialect/norm 0.2.2 per semantic-version policy, other sub-artefact versions and ISA/map/objects/hashes unchanged. title: Indirect calls in device code (R2)
description:
Audit row(s): O-01; also used by B-16, B-22, B-33
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: omission: the call graph has direct-call edges only (§4.1); §8.1 'runs host functions natively'; no lowering for CC, R or lifted code

Rungs blocked: 4, 5, 6, 7

Removal mechanism (0.2): Candidate sets for every indirect call (C1-C5 generalised; fallback as in B-33). The device closure includes all candidates. Function-address encoding: a function's address is its comparison-link address (D15). Lowering: CC/R use a compare chain or binary search over the encodings, ending in static `call @f_k`; lifted code uses `t = lift.icmp.eq fp c_k; qbranch t ^call_k ^next` with static `lift.call`. Unbounded -> reject (decision 3 analogue).

ISA 0.8 support: Yes, no change: CC `call @f` is static (ISA §4.1); `lift.call @f` is static and `qjumpr` is intra-function (ISA §4.2). Compare-and-branch is the mechanism; an indirect-call instruction would be efficiency only.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §0, §3.1 taint row, §3.2 (functions are placed by a driver-controlled comparison link whose link map the device loader replicates). Rung 4: SQLite VFS, pcache, mutex, function tables; rung 5: Julia `jl_fptr_*`; rungs 6, 7: kernel ops tables. Plan risk R2. Top-ten narrowing #4.

title: Full lifted subset in oracle regions: memory, calls, floating point, vectors (BD-E-LIFT-SUBSET)
description:
Audit row(s): D4, B-39 (and B-45 -> D16)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D4; §9.1 'Lifting of memory, calls, floating point and vectors in oracle regions'; §6.4.3

Rungs blocked: 1, 2, 4, 7, 8

Removal mechanism (0.2): Full lifted subset. loads, stores and GEPs -> `lift.boundscheck`/`lift.load`/`lift.store` (<= 128-bit pieces). Globals -> layout globals and data images; `lift.addr`. Escaping allocas -> `lift.alloc` at entry and `lift.free` at exit, or a shadow-stack global; non-escaping allocas -> locations. Allocator shim malloc/free -> `lift.alloc`/`lift.free`. Direct calls -> `lift.call`/`lift.ret` lprocs. Indirect calls -> O-01. FP -> soft-float bitcode from `bennett-arith`, lifted like any code. Vectors -> scalarisation before mapping (a normaliser rule). First-class aggregates -> per-field locations. Integers wider than 128 bits -> legalised into <= 128-bit limbs. Intrinsics: `*.with.overflow`, `*.sat`, bswap, ctpop, fshl/fshr, bitreverse, memcpy/memmove/memset -> expansions or runtime lprocs. Varargs -> O-03. Unwinding -> D10 transform. Pre-flight checks need the phase-1 interpreter.

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: ISA §4.2 rows `lift.load/store/alloc/free/call/ret/addr/boundscheck`; §3.7 stack and locations; §7.2 lifted memory; §16.3 example 2. Wide payloads: G-15.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.1 ('The ordinary loads and stores of lifted classical code (all of SQLite's) ... are lifted coherently'), §3.2 (soft-float; object-bounds model). Rung 1 only partially: any call left after O3 (Rust panic paths for / and %, Julia throw paths, non-inlined helpers) is outside the subset. Top-ten narrowing #1.

title: §13.1 zero-low tie-even parity for canonical PPC pairs (FMA and incoming IEEE conversion) (from bennett-arith-4yg.1)
description:
Source: bennett-arith/.tmp/sol-arith-softfloat/cross-repo-beads.md, "Dialect contract decision request: bennett-arith-4yg.1" (local bennett-arith-4yg.1, blocks 4yg incoming IEEE conversion/FMA conformance).

Determination: dialect 0.2.12 §13.1 specifies no tie-even parity rule for canonical double-double results whose neighbouring lows include zero, so nearest-even is undefined at zero-low transitions. Evidence: `timeout 30s python3 -u -I tests/ppc_zero_low_witness.py` in bennett-arith (success proves the witness, not conformance). Let u=2^-1074, h=1+2^-52 (f64 0x3ff0000000000001). Canonical finite inputs a=(h,u), b=(1/2,+0), c=(h/2,+0) have exact FMA h+u/2. Adjacent canonical results L=(h,+0), U=(h,u) are each distance u/2 (every pair sum is a multiple of u). The published high fallback gives L odd high parity; U has odd low significand 1; neither is even. Existing native FMA also reports flags 0 where either nearest result requires 16.

Same decision needed for incoming IEEE conversion: H = f64 raw 0x0030000000000001; V=H+2^-1075 is exactly f128 raw 0x3c030000000000001200000000000000. Adjacent canonical pairs (H,0) and (H,2^-1074) have odd/odd parity and equal distance 2^-1075. Both native conversions select the lower pair with flags 24; correct final flags are 16 because the pair total is normal.

Proposed correction: specify zero-low parity, e.g. use the low significand (zero counts as even) whenever either neighbouring low is nonzero, and high significands only when BOTH lows are zero; alternatively a deterministic equal/no-even rule. Preserve the full capability/domain; no arbitrary policy is claimed as conforming. Sqrt cannot reach this half-grid squared midpoint and is independently implemented. Related: b-dialect-spec-dfd (PPCDoubleDouble fallback vs correct rounding), bennett-arith-4yg.

title: §5.1/§5.2 need a bound on pointer offsets: the exact least fixpoint on the SQLite closure is unreachable
description: §5.1 fixes K=4096 for INT atoms only and §5 says every verdict is computed from the reference analysis, but nothing bounds explicit offsets of one object. PT2's modular orbit makes a pointer recurrence through memory, or a memcpy between offsets of one object, an ascending chain about 2^61 long, and PT6/PT7 keep one slot per (object, offset, width). Measured by bennett-plugin bp-fj1 on the rung-4 closure (N=16, 1,487 functions, LLVM 18): without a bound, 800k+ slots after round 1 and still growing. The plugin (branch rung4-plugin) therefore closes early, which is sound but coarser than the unbounded reference: (a) an AV with more than K offsets of one provenance, more than 4 offsets outside the object's literal extent, or more than 32 offsets of an object of no literal extent takes the residue class of the differences' lowest set bit plus (EXT,*) and non-handle top; (b) an object with more store-created slots than max(64, extent/4) collapses to (X,*), so PT6 gives top with explicit ROOTs kept. A verdict could only move toward rejection or a larger dispatch domain. Exact change requested: add normative offset and slot bounds beside K in §5.1, with these rules or better ones, so that a competitor's analysis reaches the same verdicts. title: Clarify PPCDoubleDouble fallback versus correct-rounding requirements

Reading B: exact high+low numerical values must be correctly rounded and extended exactly. Reproduced with same-major LLVM18/23 oracle: PPC-to-IEEE APFloat::convert/getIEEE uses the high component only, discarding even representable low components; divide/FMA/LLVM18 integral/integer operations use legacy 106-bit semantics and can discard sparse tails. LLVM23 integral/integer conversion preserves sparse tails, but positive total with a negative nonzero integral low can saturate fptoui to UINT_MAX because APFloat converts the low component to unsigned separately. Component subtraction can produce negative zero in both halves. LLVM add/mul special zero/inf sign/status behavior also differs from IEEE expectations. Neither major implements PPC sqrt. Producer chooses A for available operations, legacy-format correct sqrt otherwise, tracks conflicts rather than claiming exact IEEE double-double equivalence. Please specify priority, sqrt rounding/pair canonicalization, and constrained flags. No spec text edited.

title: Kernel and runtime platform: MMIO, interrupts, privileged state, context switch, exec, setjmp/longjmp
description:
Audit row(s): O-06 (G-16 is the efficient ISA alternative)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: omission: volatile accesses to device addresses become plain accesses by N9 and then memfault; no interrupts, address translation, stack switching, exec of user programs, setjmp/longjmp

Rungs blocked: 5, 6, 7

Removal mechanism (0.2): Needs a phase-2-style spike. Mechanisms without an ISA change: MMIO by address-range shims onto device models; interrupts by polling at loop back edges and function entries (deterministic timer from the clock model); context switch and setjmp/longjmp by an Asyncify-style transform (frames spilled to memory and rewound); user programs compiled as device code with a soft-MMU instrumentation of their loads and stores. Efficient alternative: ISA gap G-16.

ISA 0.8 support: Without G-16: yes, at large cost.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §5 (boots on the VM with its devices modelled, un-boots to the reset vector), §8 rungs 5/6/7; NS §9.11 lists setjmp as open, not excluded. Rung 6: all; rung 7: non-local exit from `panic()` to make the panic flag the payload; rung 5: Julia exceptions use sigsetjmp.

title: Taint-driven lifting of classical code under ctrl/adj/compute (coherent lifting; R1)
description:
Audit row(s): 1.4-d, D17, B-31, B-50, O-05 (all same mechanism); audit §3 TDL-1..TDL-10
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §1.4(d), §6.1 'region kind fixed by the marker', §6.6 'plugin never outlines', §8.4 (classical code of ctrl/adj/compute bodies runs once, classically), §14 D17

Rungs blocked: none directly

Removal mechanism (0.2): see audit

ISA 0.8 support: Not a dedicated ISA change. Yes: ISA §5.3 (action bodies call oracles), §4.7 `ctl w <call>` and `(args..)`, §3.3 region binding, §5.2 oracle is an involution. Efficiency items: G-13, G-14, G-15.

Why it is a narrowing / context: Does not block rungs 4/7/8 (they use the explicit `oracle` marker once D4, D21/D3, D11, B-42, O-01 are removed). Blocks NS §0 ('controlled-anything ... everything else is inferred') and the NS §5 REPL scene `when(q) do f(x) end`. Under the draft, classical stores of a ctrl body happen on both branches of q: a different result, not just a rejection. O-05 (coherent memory after a region) is part of this (TDL-4, TDL-2).


Taint-driven lifting (TDL), specifiable as dialect 0.2 rules (audit §3.2; ISA 0.8 permits it, no ISA change needed):
- TDL-1 Interface vs body. The marker fixes the region's interface (action for ctrl/adj/compute, oracle for oracle/inplace). The body is partitioned by content (TDL-3), never rejected for containing classical code (NS §4.2).
- TDL-2 Coherence lattice Cl below Co over values and (field-sensitive) abstract objects, flow-sensitive. Seeds: a store during generation of an action region to an object live after the invocation makes it Co from region exit (promotion); a load from a Co object is Co. Propagation: data dependence; control dependence (Co branch makes dependents Co, stores predicated); memory (store of Co value or under Co control makes the object Co). Interprocedural, context-sensitive, polyvariant clones per coherence signature (NS §3.1).
- TDL-3 Partition. G (generation) = Cl instructions not control-dependent on a Co branch whose stores target Cl or non-escaping objects; runs once in CC as today. Each maximal single-entry single-exit region of Co instructions is outlined (CodeExtractor) into O_k: Cl live-ins become classical args, Co live-ins input registers, Co objects read the arena region (in), Co live-outs and written bytes output targets. O_k is lifted by the D4 map; irreducible coherent code is outlined as a whole function.
- TDL-4 Coherent arena: every object that may become Co is allocated in a static range [A_coh, A_coh+2^A) of the layout, inside every oracle's [0,2^H) and disjoint from CC globals/heap (ISA §7.1/§7.2; G-13 would lift the restriction); contents in a CC-held qreg[8*2^A] bound to region[A,8] (ISA §3.3). The bennett-runtimes coherent allocator keeps bookkeeping classically; a still-Cl arena object has a CC shadow, G-code stores mirrored as basis-state updates. After promotion, CC reads of the object are a compile-time error BD-E-TAINT-HOST (host-visible outputs leave only through measurement).
- TDL-5 Events. Case A: a G store to an escaping object with classical old and new contents appends `xmask o, old^new`. Case B: each dynamic entry into slice O_k appends `oracle O_k` (args = Cl live-ins, ins = Co live-in registers, mem = arena, tgt = fresh registers for Co live-outs and new byte contents, fr = fresh wire[4]) then exchange events (`qexch` on slices for classical addresses, `qexchm` for Co addresses, ISA §4.6). Outputs wider than 128 bits are sliced (G-15).
- TDL-6 Control and adjoint: ctrl adds the control wire to every event (`ctl w`, ISA §4.7); oracle_call, qexch, qexchm and X are self-adjoint (ISA §5.3). adj of a region with escaping writes consumes the history registers of its forward invocation; without them the adjoint of a non-injective update does not exist (that case is L: NS §4.2 requires an action to be a unitary on its declared wires).
- TDL-7 History: displaced contents, per-slice fault wires, Co temporaries; lives in declared mutable wires; freed when the scheduler chooses (NS §3.1 garbage row); `compute(f, use)` frees it through adjoint(E_f). Memory is versioned, never overwritten.
- TDL-8 Faults: a final combine oracle XORs the first nonzero per-slice code into the region's declared fault register (lifted select chain).
- TDL-9 Budget: the ctrl operand or the D2 table gives (steps, heap, stack, depth) for every O_k token; exhaustion is that slice's FAULT_BUDGET_* reaching the region fault.
- TDL-10 Co control of quantum operations: a marker call control-dependent on a Co branch or with Co index/op code: an oracle computes the condition into a fresh wire and the gate is issued under `qpred` once per candidate (ISA §3.5, §4.6). A Co angle is predicated per candidate when finite, else rejected (L: NS promises predication, not superposed parameters). A Co trip count of a gate-issuing loop is padded to the budget bound, unrolled in the event list, per-iteration flags kept as history; G-14 would replace that with an action step machine.

ISA gaps: G-13 (dynamic region base), G-14 (action step machine), G-15 (wide oracle payloads) are efficiency items for ISA 0.9. ISA-4 matters for adj of a generation whose register set is known only at run time (record the event trace with its registers and replay in reverse). R1 is a dialect design task for phase 3 with no ISA blocker.

title: dialect 0.2: remove every narrowing of dialect 0.1
description:
Standing rule (bennett/docs/plan/2026-10-29-path-to-north-star.md): no narrowing of north-star scope of any kind. A deferral may postpone mechanics while keeping the capability; a default of reject/refuse/none/fault for something the north star promises is a narrowing.

Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md (phase 0, commit 3bb2ae2). 96 rows classified: N 57, M 12, L 27. 17 N rows only point at another row's mechanism, leaving 40 distinct narrowings (incl. 7 omissions O-01..O-07; O-05 is folded into the taint-driven lifting issue). Each is a child issue of this epic, labelled `narrowing` and `blocks-rung-N`.

Rungs (NS §8): 1 scalar functions; 2 pointers/structs/byte memory; 3 musl hello world; 4 Grover over SQLite; 5 Julia on a shim runtime; 6 xv6 and Linux in the reversible tier; 7 kernel fuzzing; 8 Monte Carlo amplitude estimation. Priority 0 = blocks rung 4.

title: Specify native comparison primitive exception and resolved heap configuration ABI
description:
Pinned dialect 0.2.10 @023f5a7. §19.5 says: "heap_base: the first multiple of 4096 at or after the end of the data; heap_limit_max: the largest heap of the budget table (which covers the shadow stack, §9.2)" (formatting elided). §17.7 requires materialised same-major native linkage, never host libc/libm. §3.1 says __bennett_nz_ is defined by "nobody: primitives" and reserves __bennett_rt_ definitions to runtimes plus driver __bennett_rt_blk.<f>. §14.9 defines those block objects as k-byte blockaddress identity, not heap configuration.
Reading A: primitives stay undefined in production, with a comparison-only native lowering and an explicit driver-emitted runtime configuration object conveying resolved §19.5 heap base/limit. Reading B: nobody may define primitives even in the comparison support, and the only permitted driver-defined __bennett_rt_ objects are blockaddress objects, so layout must instead travel via linker-defined symbols or an unspecified mechanism. No normative native transport ABI or allocation-record capacity is fixed.
Implementing A in brt-nuu: comparison-only native support, required external constant __bennett_rt_native_layout {u64 abi_version=1,u64 heap_base,u64 heap_limit_max}; driver emits exact resolved values after layout. Runtime maps exactly that range or faults loudly, never chooses defaults or relocates it. Allocation history capacity derived from heap_limit_max (one record per possible max(n,1) byte allocation), so no arbitrary lower limit. Reserved definitions never enter production. Please specify ownership/native exception and layout transport ABI. Driver is read-only this session and presently emits no such object.

title: Clarify musl console syscall framing and startup/model history ABI
description:
Accepted dialect 0.2.10 @023f5a7 §11.2: "`bennett-runtimes`' musl maps system calls onto the markers:" and the write/writev row. §11.3: "In an L variant, an effect marker call becomes a call of the runtimes function `__bennett_dev_<model>_<op>` with the same operands." §19.2: "a CC launch stub ... calls the R entry `<sym>` with (argc, argv, envp)". §14.7: "musl's `exit` runs the `atexit` handlers and flushes stdio, then calls `_Exit(s)`."
Two readings of console support: (A) virtual stdout/stderr are terminal-like descriptors, writev emits one console marker per nonempty vector in order, ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ) returns ENOTTY (buffered stream), seeking returns ESPIPE, and close succeeds; (B) console descriptors require an ISA expansion for terminal metadata, writev atomic framing, close and startup syscalls before musl can run. Text best supports A: only byte writes are observable, vectors preserve their byte order. Full VFS/other devices remain scope of brt-zct.
Two startup readings: (A) runtimes may publish a static single-thread musl process context and comparison-only Linux _start receiving argc/argv/envp while the driver's R entry remains main with §19.2 preparation and §14.7 exit handling; (B) every tier must enter musl's Linux ELF crt/TLS/auxv setup. A best fits the driver's explicit entry ABI, ordinary bitcode shims and no host libc.
Two tape readings: (A) the R effect tape is exclusively the ISA's, and L console globals are ordinary reversible memory (private/discarding for an oracle), with native model test undo history being test support; (B) runtimes must publish a second console tape ABI used identically in all tiers. A follows the explicit tier table; do not substitute L truncation for R tape. Need specification of optional standalone model history ABI if B intended. Action-region finite capacity must fault before mutation per TDL-12, unlike oracle truncation.

title: Per-translation-unit fast path (closed-unit mode)
description:
Audit row(s): B-54 (D23 is M; this is its companion rule)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §11.1 the plugin 'MUST do nothing in any pre-link or per-translation-unit phase'

Rungs blocked: none directly

Removal mechanism (0.2): Keep the Enzyme-PR-3211 rule for pre-link LTO phases. Add an explicit closed-unit mode (`-bennett-closed-unit`): the module is checked to have no external device callers or callees without bitcode, and is then processed exactly as a whole program.

ISA 0.8 support: n/a.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.3: a per-TU invocation remains available as a fast path for programs closed within one unit (the REPL case), with the same semantics; NS §5 REPL ('compilation is invisible, incremental').
